So after a long, long time of not playing this game, I did come back to it.
In my first review, i blasted the game for its two-bit ending to a broken story and its lack of replayability. I stand by those blastings, they hold true and you should consider them both before buying. The game doesnt have a mission replay feature (though it does have a slave slot feature so you can break away from one save path and use another in case you want to save whats ahead)
However, I was not being fair. Seeing as I had just beat it and had nothing more to do, other than taste the nasty and ugly ending in my mouth, I didnt feel like leaving it a good review. Im going to change that now to the best of my ability.
Mad max, for its weird plot hole filled story with a terrible ending, for its lack of replayability, does do one thing very, very well. It immerses you so fully in the universe it pays homage to, while still managing to be fun.
There are almost no good examples to compare it to. Most games based on films are terrible, they either try so damn hard to pay respect to the movie that they are completely unenjoyable, or they are just a first person shooter set to the music of the film with no "Feeling".
When you are driving through the desert, stopping at a salvage site in mad max, you feel paranoid about your car. You know if it runs out of fuel, if it is destroyed by passing raiders, you will die out in the desert. Its feelings like this, feelings that only desperately driving away from a gigantic sandstorm that could spell doom for you, feelings that you get when you blast some naked psychopath off the front of your car with a double barrelled sawn off shotgun, these feelings ARE mad max and this game gives you them in spades. A true videogame masterpiece immerses you in a place, a time, a circumstance much better than any movie or book could, but its much harder to achieve this. Mad Max the game does it and damn it does it well.
You look around, you see no bad guys. Gotta look around for fuel, im running on empty. You jump out of your car and scramble around looking for fuel on the ground, nothing. as you run back to your car you see a few buggies driven by lunatics coming at you, and you panic. you run for your car but they ram right into it, almost killing you with the impact of your own car flying through the air, but you dodged it, barely. As you recover the buggy charges you again, and again you dodge, quickly drawing your shotgun and putting some buckshot in the gas tank of the enemy car, blowing it to smithereens. One shell left, the other driver charges you now, and you deftly take aim, wait.. wait. With a thunderous blast you decapitate the driver with buckshot, and his buggy slips and slides at you still, one more deft dodge, and you run to his car. Low on fuel, but enough to escape, you drag the corpse out and desperately flee in the weak buggy towards a safe zone as a sandstorm bears down on you, ready to rend your flesh from your bones.
Now, granted that all of that IS possible in this game, there is one qualifying issue. Your main car comes with a sidekick, and on most of your "Missions" you are required to use it (Or worse, use a car you cant customize that the game forces you to make) and he is the little immersion breaking straw on the camels back. The devs felt that you needed a little rocket launching lunatic with a harpoon gun and a sniper rifle that can telescope open on the back of your car, in a universe where finding shotgun shells can be an impossible challenge, you have an infinite supply of rocket harpoons. This little bit is a massive letdown for me, a concession to letting people ride around in what is just a fancy fast tank. However, once you have aquired a few cars you can♥♥♥♥♥♥around in freeroam and do some objectives without him (Though many outposts require his annoying little♥♥♥♥♥. If you get in really serious trouble even in a different car you can call him with a flare too, another detracting "Feature"
I still do not rank mad max as one of my favorite games or a game id play all the time. However, I would rank it as one of the games that pulls off a movie vibe and the feelings a setting is meant to give best. Its damn good fun riding around, blowing people away with a sawn off shotgun, brutally fighting enemies with what feels like a batman:arkham series melee system. It is a fun game, I do enjoy playing it. The story was so close to being amazing, but a few poor development choices (For instance, some plot points are only shown in side missions which are optional, so you may come back to do a side mission only to see story characters who are dead or gone back in their spots. Or you may play the main game and see someone who was introduced and explained in a side mission you never did) And an ending that tries waayyy too hard to be deep and painful, means the story gets low marks from me. All the same, the combat and car gameplay are superb and fun (Most of the time) and I do recommend you pick this up if you are a mad max fan or just really like feeling immersed in a good setting.
People like me who love violence and sawn off shotguns will feel at home with this game.

Two years after its release, Spec Ops: The Line remains as the most mature presentation of War in video gaming. Comparing it to CoD and Battlefield, the two hype train every year, Spec Ops tell deep narratives about the horrors / attrocities of war while also presenting the player with decisions that provide no black and white outcome, as it should.
Spec Ops graphics greatly beats Battle Field graphics, its not really about the engine, due to the things that they show. Take a frag grenade. Dust from Frags in Battlefield and CoD dissipate in about 1-3 seconds; while in Spec Ops, they remain for up to 5-7 seconds, completely blinding the players to the features of the enemy AI. Prison Architect is a tycoon game. You have to build and maintain your own prison. So you build cell blocks, kitchens, yards ect. Very simple, but extremly addictive - my first try took roughly around 8h - rare even for me.
You will have to deal with situations typical for prisons, like riots, prisoners attacing each other or your staff, escapes... But lets star from the beggining.
Tutorial isn't long, but it shows the basics just fine. After playing it, you should be able to build your own prison. You have 24 game hours before inmates arrival, abd by then you have to build basic facilities - like few cells, kitchen, offices, ect. Important thing is, that you need to think ahead. Careless expanding electrical lines may cause your generator to get overloaded, and that leads to energy shortage in whole prison. You also need to take care of risk, because the higher it is, the bigger chances are that your prisoners will do something stupid - what will affect your income. So you need to take care of their needs, don't infract their laws (lockdowns without reasons, or reasonless seraches are problem). They need to have good food, comfort, entertainment, and safety (so hiring too much ared guards will make them angrier), which is a bit too good for such scoundrels, isn't it? With game progress, you can unlock more features, like hiring K9 unit (guards with dogs), education, prison labour (making prisoners work for you), and so on.
Game features much more things (like inteligence, allowing you to intercept contraband, and more), but writing about it would be pointless. This review would be too long, and that's not the point. So lets say about good and bad sides. Good thing is, that game is still in early access, and it's current form is great alredy. Playing it is (mostly) entertainging, but still there are some things that could be added, or improved. Theese are bad things: workers sometimes pass through the walls, you cant allow workers to open jail doors (so they need to wait for guard to come and open it, or for player to change door setting), or doctors  need to be sent to patients, not other way - which annoys me terribly, because if you wont notice that someone needs a doctor, he will die. And this doctor stays in his office. There should be a possibility to at least make him wander around the prison and heal everyone who needs it - and currently, you need to look for wounded prisoners/staff and send him to them. Apart of this, game is worth playing.

Black Ops II is NOT a bad game. Let me just establish that from the start. Contrary to popular belief, BO2 brings many new innovations which the franchise has been lacking since Modern Warfare 2. The campaign is very different in its story. Zombies has been expanded beyond anyone's imagination. And multiplayer has received a complete overhaul. With a great selection of game modes, weapons, perks, equipment, scorestreaks, customisation options etc. as well as League Play where everything is unlocked, it's hard to fault it. However, I can give many reasons why this doesn't make the game exciting at all. Sure, create-a-class offers total freedom without pre-set restrictions, but in reality your playstyle is not respected within the game itself. While the weapons are generally balanced, the sheer pace of the game means shotguns and SMGs have the upper hand in most situations. Whilst the choice of weapons and class options are there, barely any of it is actually useful. With all the new stuff I feel that the game is too cluttered. There is a lot of rubbish around, yet the game doesn't feel fresh or exciting even though it's almost completely different. The controls feel somewhat odd relative to the pacing and map design, so it's not like previous Call of Duty games where all class setups would be appropriate for all maps. The multiplayer is fun for about an hour, after that it's plain boring, not satisfying at all. Campaign is commendable for trying to bring new ideas but ultimately fails to deliver compared to Modern Warfare 3's campaign. BO2's campaign is not only unnecessarily complicated and difficult to follow, but the gameplay in it is very boring and not intense even on Veteran difficulty. Zombies has gone completely mental. No longer is it a simple horde mode in confined areas; rather it's more about finding easter eggs and following lengthy guides just to figure out where you can buy a perk or upgrade your weapon. Overall, Black Ops II seems self-defeating in a way. It aims to create a competitive multiplayer yet provides anti-competitive tools rather than focusing on pure skill, regardless of choice of class. Yet with zombies, it's clearly aimed at little kids who enjoy bragging about finding new stuff in a game. I must say, I'm disappointed that even a CoD game which brings so much new stuff fails to be more exciting than Modern Warfare 3.

At first glance Spec Ops: The Line seems like an average modern military third-person shooter with a cover system. And that assessment is largely correct. It feels and plays a lot like Call of Duty and Battlefield singleplayer campaigns, mainly due to its action-movie style setpieces. This despite it being a third-person cover shooter.
Even so Spec Ops: The Line is one of the better singleplayer shooters you can pick up today. It's not a standout in visuals, bombastic action scenes, shooting mechanics, or multiplayer options. Rather it sets itself apart due to the atmosphere set in the singleplayer story, the gruesome choices you're forced to make, the cruel twists as the story moves along, and some horrific scenes of brutality.
You get to make only a few choices during the campaign and Spec Ops' environments are linear throughout. But those choices you do get to make have an impact - not so much on the game's story as on you as a person due to their immediate effects. Additionally the game comes with several different endings. There's no need to replay the game for them, because the decision that determines which ending you get is made in the final mission, which is both sad yet convenient.
At 6-7 hours the game never overstays its welcome. Likewise it's never overly challenging, and that's on Hard (Suicide Mission) difficulty. That short, mostly-linear campaign holds up surprisingly well in a second playthrough. Finding all the nuances that point to the game's final twists further enhances the experience.
Spec Ops is not a fun game. But it's one hell of an experience for those who can handle a bit of grimdarkness in their third-person shooting. Definitely recommended.

Brilliant game, wonderful and insightful commentary on the tropes of first person shooters and the morality of conflict as a whole. By the end of the game, I was hating myself for what had simply seemed natural at the time.
Let me qualify this, however, by saying that the game does box you into some of the "choices" you make. Where the game's intended plotline does not coincide with your actual wishes, there's a distinct dissonance that can lead to blaming the game rather than yourself, as I think was probably intended.
Addionally, the gameplay was rather frustrating and not very well designed. I would often end up repeating certain segments again and again simply because of lack of cover, clunky controls, or unclear sources of damage. One segment, in which there was a helicopter shooting in through a window that had to be avoided, I ended up repeating over and over simply because I couldn't tell where it was shooting (where I could run) and nothing seemed to be working. In the end, I got through by pure chance. Also, these sections would frequently be in the vicinity of a cutscene (which would have to be rewatched every time), or at least take a rather large amount of time to reload, which contributed to an overall feeling of extreme frustration at times.
Overall, do play this game, and do try to play it through to completion, but perhaps choose one of the easier difficulties to avoid the experience being ruined by poor gameplay design.

Rogue Legacy is your basic hack-n-slash rogue game. While it has a lot of mechanics, and a lot of unlockable equipment, it's downfall is how repetative the game seems.
You start off as a character (your choice of three randomly generated characters) and explore a tomb-like game. There are four distinct areas of the game, as well as a respective boss for each area
.
The game plays out evolution-style, where you can't really do a lot comfortably (although there are videos of people completing bosses at level 1), but as you collect gold, you slowly build up your castle, and unlock upgrades and new equipment.
After completing the game a few times, it felt like a grind to keep going. There is no reason to complete the game multiple times aside from bragging rights, and there wasn't much of a reason to keep playing, aside from achievements.
I'd definitely place this game as a "I need to kill some time" game, and would only recommend it as such. There is no captivating story to keep you here, and I wouldn't expect anybody to put in nearly the amount of hours I did, for fun or otherwise.

The goal of the game is to beat every single section boss, ( There is 4 sections, the castle, the forest, the maya and the darkness. After beating everysingle section boss, the golden door at the beginning of the castle will open and reveal the final boss, The Traitor after defeating him, The Fountain comes fourth, kill him and you win the game.
There is remixes of all the 4 section bosses which are considerably harder.
It's a fun game, and if you need some singleplayer action, look no further, than Rogue Legacy.

Prison Architect... is an awesome game.

I love this game, and to still call in 'early access' is almost a joke. This could easily be sold as a full game in its current state and I'd be totally happy with that.
This is a god-interaction game in which you send builders in to build the foundations and walls of your prison, delegate the furniture, pick what 'upgrades' you want (CCTV, hightened security, informants, and much more) if you have the money, decide the routine (time to sleep, time to eat, time to work, time to sit in your cell and be bored) etc.
You can manage it right down to the quality of their meals. Plan the staff, give them dedicated routes, automatically increase the security at high risk times such as meal times or free time.
If you want to play the standard mode then you have to work with the budget you have. Take on contracts to boost your pot and increase your prison. Are you a labour-driven workaholic who focuses only on his prisoners suffering? Or are you a 'second chance' person who equips their prisoners with knowledge and gives them the tools to prepare them for returning to a working society?
If you ever get bored of the standard mode, drop by the PA Steam Workshop and pick up new elements of gameplay - make your prisoners work a vegetable patch as well as the standard workshop, open up a mil sorting office to give postal happiness to prisoners and staff alike, or subscribe to the 'sandbox mode' mod which opens up a basic starter plot with $999,999,999,999 and lets you on your way.
I love PA - I recommend it to everyone.

Prison Architect is awesome.  It's a great simulator game in the vein of Sim City, but much more unusual.  I'm a pretty casual player, but I can play without feeling stifled or pathetic.  When I look at what more hardcore players have accomplished, it's pretty amazing.
The best part of Prison Architect is that it's constantly getting better.  This is pretty much the ideal Early Access Game.  Every month there's a new release with great improvements and a really good video explaining them all.  I hope the game's never complete!
One of my favorites for sure.

Prison Architect is not your average sandbox game.  You have to build, budgeting all the way, realize you went over budget, and then curse under your breath as you press the menu button.
Once you finally have a prison going, including the cost of staff, your prison is open! Aaaaaaand within a day there's a riot. Grumbling under your breath even louder, you now restart, but with unlimited funds.
Your prison become a nationwide acknowledged facility.
10/10

Having played it so much, the design aspect of the prison can often feel more like work then fun, but yet I often keep doing it as at the end it is fun seeing if your new idea will actually work once the inmates come in. To me that is the best way to describe Prison Architect.
As they continue to update the ease of running the prison has become harder and thus made the game even more enjoyable when you get to that aspect. My last prison, the general formula I've used over numerous alphas was seriously tested as tunneling was becoming the newest prisoner past time. In another there were a few issues with deaths and fights breaking out that had not been experienced before, later finding out that the issue was we had a snitch and well...things did not go well for him.
Getting a bit off topic but what you get is an enjoyable game if you like builder type strategy games, like the mentioned Bullfrog games or games like Restaurant Empire and such. Not totally bug free but much more so then many Early Access titles, and with another bit of bug bashing Introversion could cut development and release it and you'd have an already good title. However, thankfully, they continue to add more content and make the game even more enjoyable and better.

I dont really know what to say about this game, but here's a delicious chocolate cake recipe.
:INGREDIENTS FOR CAKE:
2 cups white sugar
1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
1 1/2 teaspoons baking soda
1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder
1 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1 cup milk
1/2 cup vegetable oil
:INGREDIENTS FOR FROSTING:
2 teaspoons vanilla extract
1 cup boiling water
3/4 cup butter
1 1/2 cups unsweetened cocoa powder
5 1/3 cups confectioners' sugar
2/3 cup milk
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
:INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour two 9 inch cake pans.
2. Use the first set of ingredients to make the cake. In a medium bowl, stir together the sugar, flour, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt. Add the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla, mix for 3 minutes with an electric mixer. Stir in the boiling water by hand. Pour evenly into the two prepared pans.
3. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes in the preheated oven, until a toothpick inserted comes out clean. Cool for 10 minutes before removing from pans to cool completely.
4.To make the frosting, use the second set of ingredients. Cream butter until light and fluffy. Stir in the cocoa and confectioners' sugar alternately with the milk and vanilla. Beat to a spreading consistency.
5. Split the layers of cooled cake horizontally, cover the top of each layer with frosting, then stack them onto a serving plate. Frost the outside of the cake.

tl;dr
Lets star with
Now, get Farcry. Strip it of all the mildly interesting side missions and all of the fun ways of getting from one place to another and limit it to a bunch of cars that don't look that different to each other (and except for the main car, most of the adquired enemy cars are crap, so there's no real reason to drive them except to add them to the collection).
Some people compare it with the Batman games. I'm not a Fan of those ones either (neither Assasins creed, but have played them plenty) but it seems to me that the Batman games have more flavor because of the stealth.
The fighting is incredibly boring to perform, but fun to watch. The whole combat is done with two buttons basically: attack and parry. Now you just have to time them to the icons on the screen. Matter little where your character is facing. So skill needed for this game? Zero. A monkey can play.
.
. Gas is irrelevant and abundant. After a couple hours, you will be refilled for free at the main fortresses. You eat and drink to replenish a life bar that does not matter much. I died 8 times in 20 hours of gameplay. 7 of them where because I fell off a cliff trying to get to the car quicker. The other one because I stopped looking at the screen in the middle of a battle while I was having a conversation. Even with that, it took me an incredible amount of time to die and pretty much every body was dead by then. So No survival, Zero challenge.
Everything you can interact with physically (climbing, passing through) it's marked in bright yellow paint, just in case you IQ is under 40, so you know exactly where to go. Even the so called "secret entrances". Bright yellow signalized secret entrances.
There's also this whole mechanic used in assassin's creed and Farcry of having to climb towers to reveal map. You have it here too. Except it's a balloon. And it's incredibly slow. Why do they keep making these climbing things? They are terribly boring.
And talking about terribly boring, you have the sand storms. The first time seems cool. So immersive, woaaa. But after that one time, it consists on staying by the boxes with loot and wait about 5 min parked, without being able to leave the car, just to collect the crates. Who thought that was fun?
All the things people say there are to do? Lies. There are multiple mini missions, small quests, yes, but there are only like 7 different ones, repeated (many multiple times) in a different location. I understand this could be said even of games like Skyrim, but the difference is that those worlds are filled with hundreds of interesting NPCs doing their own thing. Here you might find the same group of NPC who need water. Give it to them. Quest done.
There must be about 7 different missions:
That's pretty much it.
And the NPCs? Poorly acted, repeating the same lines over and over (in the case of the wanderers that they only want your fat misty canteen) and a couple of bad guys, spawned out of nowhere, either in a car, or hanging out in small groups by the road (you can just pass by and wave from your desk chair as they will be out of sight before they even react). Only the few main characters have decent voice acting. There's also a girl in the game with perfectly applied nail polish, Poor design choice.
I've played it out of despise. It seems like with 20 hours in the game, if I'm not done with the game, the duration is long. Well, that's just an illusion. It's long because it take forever driving across a desert of nothingness to get to one point to another to do all these crappy repetitive missions. Of those 20 hours probably 16 are driving from one point to another without much action and 1h of cinematics. The rest is doing the same thing over and over (go to a location, fight the bad guys, collect all the loot and destroy all the insignias) Most of the time has been spent looking for the stupid insignias and loot to get a 100% completion in the area.
After a couple hours of upgrades, no enemy stand a chance and they become a nuisance. The only enjoyment is like the senseless violence and the beautifully rendered explosions.
You know you get a dog? That sounds cool, right?. Except it's not. The dog is tied to a crappy vehicle that is only good to take him to the mine fields. He does not leave the car, just barks in the direction there's a mine, you step out of the car, press E, an unskipable animation (exactly the same every time) plays and the mine is off. Fortunately, there's only 3 mines per field. 2 more than it should. It's usually more fun to drive over and make them detonate. You might even die! and at least, you don't have to wait for a sensless animation.
The
?
Good Graphics (it does look really cool in fact). and well optimized. For me, not enough to recommend this to anyone. You want HD wonderful graphics? look through your window with a pair of polarized glasses. Now, that' stunning HD.
I deeply regret paying 60 bucks for this. I wish I could get a refund.
If you can buy it for 20 or less (and you could, even before this Chinese New Year sale, wish I had known), I would give it a go. Otherwise, I can't recommend it.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

Truth be told, I am not a huge fan of Roguelike games on a whole. Despite their mechanical purity and focus on strong gameplay, they often suffer from poor level design and a lack of emotional connection or progression. Rogue Legacy, however, manages to subvert the latter in a very intriguing way, even if I feel that many of the more negative trappings of Roguelike games haunt this title.
The game continues to suffer from the poor level design of its contemporaries. Being a Metroidvania inspired title, with a massive vania and a small sobbing Metroid being dragged along with it, this isn't as big of an issue as it could be. But in a genre which so clearly has great level design laid out for it, it would've easily been possible to make this game have fantastic level design, due to the way it randomizes levels. At current, it has large amounts of enemy spam and doesn't really let you take advantage of your characters' particular abilities very well, aside from the base core mechanics.
Unlike other Metroidvania titles, this game doesn't introduce new weapons or game mechanics as you progress through the game, but linear upgrades like higher HP stats, strength, and different classes whom usually have a unique ability not directly related to combat or movement, and shuffled stats. The game's character progression is relatively weak, is what I'm saying.
But despite suffering from weak character progression and poor level design, this game has a certain permanence to your actions which other roguelikes don't. Your upgrades and unlocks stay with you as you play. Even with what is ostensibly the game's prestige mode, old upgrades and traits are kept and even enhanced. It culminates in a very enjoyable experience where you never necessarily feel like you've 'lost' much outside of the dungeons resetting, and you can pick up the game and continue right from where you left off again.
In terms of game design, this is a rather poor title, but it participates in filling the niche of a more replayable game following the core concepts of Metroidvania style action platforming. A niche which was previously very empty.
If the idea of a Metroidvania game which focuses on replayability sounds good to you, even if it has fairly poor level design and a progression system that leaves me lukewarm to it, it's very much so worth a try.
I look forward to seeing the future offerings of Cellar Door Games. It's rumored that they're planning to start work on a Rogue Legacy sequel in the future, to which I would say that it should basically be this, with a more varied progression system featuring more substantial changes to movement mechanics and weapons, along with more stark level design, potentially killing the 'castle' segments altogether.
But as it stands, this game fills both a unique niche, and one with very wide appeal. It is worth playing in many senses of the word, but with clear flaws and a lack of polish regarding many of the core ideas.

Good for eliminating bosses since they cannot move or shoot while active. The Commando: Can build a sentry turret. Good for clearing out waves of enemies. Finally, The Gunzerker: Can dual-wield any weapon in the game. Good for taking out enemies with far superior levels than you.
3) Guns. There are over a billion guns in the game. Ranging from Normal to Legendary. I forget the rarity color legend though. But I think it has over 6 qualities.

Not all bosses respawn, but most of them do. Only the main bosses don't respawn, such as W4R-D3N, Bloodwing, Gluttonous Thresher, and so on.
And finally, 5) Goliaths. I absoulutely LOOOOOOOOVE leveling up Goliaths. For those of you who don't know what I'm talking about, I'll tell you. Goliaths are big, bulky behemoths with masks on them. Shoot of the mask, and they go on a frenzy, killing everyone in sight. They don't use their guns, luckily, so they can't really kill you unless you're too close.
If they kill someone, they level up. And each level they get, they need an extra kill to level up again. I love getting those Fatal GOD-liaths to just f**k up everyone in sight.
In my opinion, 11/10 IGN. Get this game NOW.

An absolute gem of a construction/simulation game! Even if it's in Early Access, I would say it's better than some games which have been full released, though this of course, is very subjective. Still though, the concept is incredibly fun and amusing, even though... you're constructing a prison for some hardened prisoners? Particularly in Early Access, you can also come across some bugs, but that's fine, Introversion is doing a great job working on the game, and ironing out these bugs while also adding more new features.
The game has a bit of a learning curve, with only a very brief introduction before throwing you into the deep end. Why doesn't this or that work? But that's fine, you can only learn from your mistakes after all. Your prisoners have escaped because you locked your doors open? You forgot to build a perimeter wall? Your kitchen is too small to feed your prisoners? Well, you've learnt from your first mistake, your next prison will be much better! It's incredible just how quickly time slips by when you're building your own prison.
The sandbox nature of the game is incredible. Even at this early stage, you are given many options with which to construct and expand your prison. Do you allow or deny your prisoners comfort? Don't worry though, their cells must be indoors and have a bed and a toilet... But the possibilities are virtually endless. You can give cells bookshelves, or windows. You can make paths between different rooms and buildings of your prison. There are a huge number of different rooms and objects you can place to improve your prison, which only makes the game much more fun and interesting.
But that's not all! You manage your prison as you construct it, hiring staff (most importantly, builders to you know, build your prison), keeping your prisoners contained and reasonably happy, and completing your To-Do List. It can take a bit of work to figure out what you're doing wrong and what is going right, but the path is always an enjoyable one. Something that is only made better by the Steam Workshop support, offering incredible replayability with mods if you so choose - not that you really need to in order to sink many, many hours into this beauty.

Not one of best COD titles but playable game, I play only multiplayer have about 1100 hours on record.
First of all lets start with primary things we all want to hear about, game play. This is done pretty much as in all other games, mostly great. Many people call some guns overpowered but I don't think so. Sure, AN and MP7 are preferable guns for most players, but in my opinion, once you master all guns you can find the one that suits you best and you won't be in disadvantage vs. those guns. After all, some prefer precision, some prefer shorter/longer range, someone likes mobility better etc. Knives in this game are really lousy. Yeah it kills after one stab, but you need to try your best to stab someone. It's not enough to stand next to somebody in perfect position because sometimes you won't get a kill. And knife swing!!! Take a normal knife and try to swing in in empty. It takes about half a second before you can swing again. But our character is pretty stupid. Because with ballistic knifes (always) and sometimes with normal knifes he decides to stab instead of cut so it takes him about 2 sec to be ready for attack again (also already mentioned bug that you see your knifes in somebody's back without him being dead). Sniper shooting is more or less OK, but you will definitely see problems with ballista. Quite often one shot in the chest won't kill enemy at first while sometimes he will be dead from one shot bellow. Quickscoping can be mastered to level that you can be better at close range than guys with smg. Rocket launchers have absolutely no precision at medium distance and further, and are easily stopped with flak jackets but useful against air targets. EMP grenade works much better for ground. Shotguns are also very useful at close range with exception of KSG which is more like a sniper. Best if you are good at aim, worst if you aren't. Unlike last Blackops, you can have more than one perk instead of tactical or lethal. Most of great players use 4 or even 5 perks instead of using secondary gun or extra equipment. Also, there are quite a few fun games at party mix. However you can't choose all modes in normal and hard core mode which is great minus. Spawn system also sucks in most types of games. There are predetermined spots which you can camp easily. If you put a guardian or sentry gun near one spawn spot they won't spawn there so you can easily put 2 or 3 pieces and spawn camp. But sometimes you don't spawn in that places but in enemy base (for example in CTF). Why you can't spawn on other side of the every time when 6 of them are in your base I have no idea!!!
Secondly, I would like to talk about servers and game finding options. It sucks big time. If I need to grade it from 1 to 100 i would rate it 2. And that's only because it eventually finds a game. There is absolutely no good word for that. Once you decide to join a game first you see number of how many people are playing the game. Of course, number is same after you few times join and leave the lobby. Often the number is 3-5 (not enough people to even start a game) and yet you join completely empty lobby. When you choose to find a game it takes up to 10 seconds to search for lobby and searching quality for 50 games that don't exist before it actually starts to look through games that are there. If there is more than one game you have no chance of choosing which to join. Even after you exit the lobby and search for game again it will put you in the same lobby many times before it might give you chance to join another. Also, sometimes when you wait in lobby it will automatically transfer you to some other lobby that has people in it. Of course, in 90% of cases you DON'T want that. Why? Simple, not all the people own expansion packs and even if 9 out of 12 people do and want to play expansion maps, you will be transfered to regular maps. Sometimes you are in lobby with 5 people waiting for 1 to start and it transfers you to other lobby of only 3 people (and not in expansion maps). If you try to exit and find game you were in you will succeed if you try million times in 50% of cases.
Lag is another great problem in game. Difference between 60 and 90 lag gives a bit advantage while a difference of about 100 gives a great advantage to player with lesser lag. And just because it says your lag is 90 doesn't mean you will have a smooth game. Quite often lag is greater because of the server. Of course, you can't see or affect this so sometimes it's just better to leave. Too often you just disconnect from Steam and a little less from BO2 servers.
So all in all, the game is good with some minor gameplay issues but there are major problems everything else. I think grade of 72 or 73 that was given to it by official Steam grading is ok. First Blackops is far better game for me.

Pros : Car Combat and Car customization are absolutely phenomenal! There's nothing more satisfying than driving around, encountering a convoy, and after a long and arduous pursuit.. being able to claim your hood ornament.

Pros : Your sidekick. I'm sure you've allready heard about your hilarious sidekick thats always there to help you with some witty religious comments relating to cars.
Pros : It runs INCREDIBLY well and looks amazing. This is a game that will actually let you use your beautiful new 2k monitor and will easily run at above 60fps.
Cons : Boring MIssion Stucture. This game suffers from the classic problem that most open world suffer from. Boring missions and a world that is filled with repetitive activities. Most side missions include taking over bases or grabbing certain items. It quickly becomes fairly boring.
Cons/Pros : This will depend but alot of people thought the hand to hand combat was quite shallow. Its an arkham style hand to hand combat with bery few combos that shake up the combat. I, personally, didn't mind it, even though it felt like it was missing some spark.
Final Verdict : I recommend. Maybe not at full price but at a 50 to 66% discount I absolutely recommend it. Theres some great set pieces, amazing car combat and it runs like no other game on PC. If you saw the Mad Max : Fury Road and enjoyed it, don't skip this great game.

This game feels like a successor to the Rainbox Six: Vegas line, employing many of the same 3-man, cover-based strategies. A great blend of action and decent storytelling, Spec Ops: The Line suffers from one crippling failure, that the "cover" and "sprint" buttons are blended into one, making both actions clunky and HIGHLY prone to failure. A better control scheme would make this one of the more exciting shooters available, but as it is the game is frustrating and a perfect example of a dev team failing to understand one of the core elements of their own genre. If the devs ever patch this dumbfounding oversight I'd recommend this game 100%. Until then, save your money and just pick up R6 Vegas and Vegas II instead.

Not one of best COD titles but playable game, I play only multiplayer have about 1100 hours on record.
First of all lets start with primary things we all want to hear about, game play. This is done pretty much as in all other games, mostly great. Many people call some guns overpowered but I don't think so. Sure, AN and MP7 are preferable guns for most players, but in my opinion, once you master all guns you can find the one that suits you best and you won't be in disadvantage vs. those guns. After all, some prefer precision, some prefer shorter/longer range, someone likes mobility better etc. Knives in this game are really lousy. Yeah it kills after one stab, but you need to try your best to stab someone. It's not enough to stand next to somebody in perfect position because sometimes you won't get a kill. And knife swing!!! Take a normal knife and try to swing in in empty. It takes about half a second before you can swing again. But our character is pretty stupid. Because with ballistic knifes (always) and sometimes with normal knifes he decides to stab instead of cut so it takes him about 2 sec to be ready for attack again (also already mentioned bug that you see your knifes in somebody's back without him being dead). Sniper shooting is more or less OK, but you will definitely see problems with ballista. Quite often one shot in the chest won't kill enemy at first while sometimes he will be dead from one shot bellow. Quickscoping can be mastered to level that you can be better at close range than guys with smg. Rocket launchers have absolutely no precision at medium distance and further, and are easily stopped with flak jackets but useful against air targets. EMP grenade works much better for ground. Shotguns are also very useful at close range with exception of KSG which is more like a sniper. Best if you are good at aim, worst if you aren't. Unlike last Blackops, you can have more than one perk instead of tactical or lethal. Most of great players use 4 or even 5 perks instead of using secondary gun or extra equipment. Also, there are quite a few fun games at party mix. However you can't choose all modes in normal and hard core mode which is great minus. Spawn system also sucks in most types of games. There are predetermined spots which you can camp easily. If you put a guardian or sentry gun near one spawn spot they won't spawn there so you can easily put 2 or 3 pieces and spawn camp. But sometimes you don't spawn in that places but in enemy base (for example in CTF). Why you can't spawn on other side of the every time when 6 of them are in your base I have no idea!!!
Secondly, I would like to talk about servers and game finding options. It sucks big time. If I need to grade it from 1 to 100 i would rate it 2. And that's only because it eventually finds a game. There is absolutely no good word for that. Once you decide to join a game first you see number of how many people are playing the game. Of course, number is same after you few times join and leave the lobby. Often the number is 3-5 (not enough people to even start a game) and yet you join completely empty lobby. When you choose to find a game it takes up to 10 seconds to search for lobby and searching quality for 50 games that don't exist before it actually starts to look through games that are there. If there is more than one game you have no chance of choosing which to join. Even after you exit the lobby and search for game again it will put you in the same lobby many times before it might give you chance to join another. Also, sometimes when you wait in lobby it will automatically transfer you to some other lobby that has people in it. Of course, in 90% of cases you DON'T want that. Why? Simple, not all the people own expansion packs and even if 9 out of 12 people do and want to play expansion maps, you will be transfered to regular maps. Sometimes you are in lobby with 5 people waiting for 1 to start and it transfers you to other lobby of only 3 people (and not in expansion maps). If you try to exit and find game you were in you will succeed if you try million times in 50% of cases.
Lag is another great problem in game. Difference between 60 and 90 lag gives a bit advantage while a difference of about 100 gives a great advantage to player with lesser lag. And just because it says your lag is 90 doesn't mean you will have a smooth game. Quite often lag is greater because of the server. Of course, you can't see or affect this so sometimes it's just better to leave. Too often you just disconnect from Steam and a little less from BO2 servers.
So all in all, the game is good with some minor gameplay issues but there are major problems everything else. I think grade of 72 or 73 that was given to it by official Steam grading is ok. First Blackops is far better game for me.

Well DayZ, this review has been a long time coming- and it's finally here.
I bought this game as soon as it hit steam, oh and the joy in my heart when it did. A subtle but satisfying personal Christmas gift I got for myself. I can honestly say I prefer the game it was then, than it is now. Not because it ran any better, or had less bugs. No, it was the sunny optimism behind supporting a game that was right up my alley. If you want a recommendation before I go into my spiel then here it is- No, I do not recommend buying this game. My explanation for that is as follows:
I've had so many good times with this game, a couple hundred hours of exciting gameplay manifested itself in the form of a relatively simple concept. There is no story, there is no "end game", there is no main objective. Except that of Survival. That's what hooked me, and what hooked many others like me. The possibilities are endless in this game, and because of the shoot-on-sight community, your survival is secured by how cold hearted you can be. Now, that never stopped me from helping fellow players. I've done everything from feeding a starving survivor to hitting a half dead waster with defibrillator and giving him a blood transfusion, just to keep him alive a little longer in that harsh world. That being said: I've also had to execute a few bandits, leave some survivors in handcuffs and penny-less in a zombie infested town, and even got my revenge on a hostile player by forcing him to eat his dead comrade. Life in DayZ is a bittersweet symphony that is played by an underground rock band that hipsters pretend to love. Truly the game has so much damn potential it almost brings tears to my eyes to not give it a recommendation. That brings me to the negatives...
I had to explain what I love about the game so you can understand why I can no longer help support it's sales. Numero Uno, The Developers. They made this game on one of the most popular mods in gaming history, DayZ mod for Arma 2. Though it's almost like they couldn't handle a stand alone development, and after releasing an early access game decided to spend their fortune of success instead of making a great game out of the shell. It's been 3 long years of Alpha and no real release in sight. Though, why would they work on a release? Players like me already gave them their money, why waste more time on a few more sales? That's what I feel like the Developers are saying to one another. "We already made our money" Now the community that's left is stuck waiting on the final product, being strung along by small updates and hot fixes. It's a damn shame. That's only the tip of this dirty Iceberg.
Let's talk about how the game plays. Your character is the hungriest and thirstiest son of a gun on the planet. The average human can go up to three weeks without food, and 3 days without water. Your survivor can't go more than an hour on an empty stomach. That is probably my biggest issue with the game, along with the zombies. The zombie AI is glitchy, sometimes they'll notice you from 200 yards away sometimes they can't see you unless you walk right up to them. They can walk through doors that you close behind you for a quick getaway, and they are built like a tank. You can nail a player without a helmet in the noggin with a crowbar and he's out, but a zombie will take 3-4 hits. If those two aspects didn't make the game almost unplayable, the loot system does. The hunting aspect of theHunter: CotW is a lot of fun, but I have spent hours simply walking through the GORGEOUS environments! Take the time to explore the game world; just like the real world, there are beautiful spots in some of the least expected places. The development team clearly put a lot of time and effort into the environment.

Really, the outdoors experience in this open world sand box hunting sim is so like being in the great outdoors that most sessions I forget I’m gaming. I often even forget the fact that I’m looking for achievements in the game. And, for a gamer who enjoys the thrill of capturing every single achievie, that’s a big deal. It is the total world immersion that makes the experience of COTW so impressive. I’ve only been playing for 3 weeks, but at the time of writing the review I have 60% of the achievements and almost 200 hours in game. I am already the ‘Hero of Hirschfelden’ and ‘Lord of the Lakes’ because I’ve explored the total area of both maps. (*Mumbles to self in monologue-ing voice: “I like that. Yes I like that very much.”) The missions are challenging enough that it will be awhile before I finish them all. So, time in game is almost unlimited. I can’t see a stopping point yet.

I often think of the game as a mountain climbing sim with hunting opportunities. Of course, that’s because I’ve often wished for a sim for climbing mountains. And, the challenge of discovering all the sights modeled after real-life geographical landforms: archipelago, butte, canyon, gorge, volcano, and much more, is all very alluring. But, many natural points of interest are integrated into the maps, providing a history or lore to these fictional maps that matches their real-life counterparts. You are able to climb every mountain in the game. You can explore totem memorials and abandoned ruins and collect artifacts. The sound effects immerse you in the outdoor world, and the music is lovely. Every area of the map is crafted with painstaking detail that provides eye-catching splendor to each sunrise and sunset.
Much of the fun gameplay comes in with tracking the animals, for hunting and for photography with the cinematic camera in the controls. The controls are all very simple, and can be keymapped for ease of use. I like the run toggle so you don’t have to hold down W. I changed the E use key to mouse 5, so that when I’m tracking I can run toggle and use the mouse to navigate and click to read the tracks as I’m running. The overlay provides mapping and a codex that stores all your accumulated knowledge of the world you’ve discovered.
The day/night cycle is 4 times the speed of in real life. So you have 3 real time hours of darkness to immerse in the nightlife of the woods, as well as those daytime hours. Many outposts are scattered throughout the maps, and provide access to your storage, the in-game store, and a sleep point. Sleeping allows you to move time ahead in hours. Setting it to 18:00 for example, would make it sundown if you want to hunt at night. But, each time you sleep costs in-game money, making it a bit more of a challenge.
Your character and your atv can take damage. Creatures stampede and can hurt you. But, ‘death’ only resets your character at a sleep point & you lose nothing. Atvs are unlimited. Abandoning one at the foot of a mountain is nothing. You can retrieve it at the next outpost, or even pitch a tent, and summon one up. Tents have a limit that seems to be about 7 or so on each reserve. With fast travel, you are able to move from tent to tent if you wanted to be in another location to hunt at dark. I like to explore in the daytime, and hunt at sunset, sunrise, and nighttime.
Throughout the world you come across animal need zones and tracks. These can be ‘read’ to give information about when the animal species was last there and often how many animals were in that location. Returning to that spot at the same time will allow you to encounter that species, whether for hunting or photography. Multiple arcs of missions are imbedded in the single player to allow the option of structured gameplay, for those who want more than just simple run and gun type game play. Of course, even the most hobbit-like adventurers like me, who love to wander around the countryside seeing all the sites and animals, love to find a cozy spot on a rock overlooking a canyon and accumulate a few carcasses down below before climbing down to harvest them all.

COTW has a range of weapons that you feel sufficiently motivated to collect for hunting every species. Of course, more is always better, when it comes to weapons in game. More would be even better. It also has lures, ammo, and other gear for hunting. Scattered around the countryside are woodpiles for building permanent ground blinds using in-game currency. These provide more experience points for the skills & perk trees as well. The skill & perk trees provide a good range of skills to work toward increased hunting experience for the current 60 max of levels. These add abilities such as gauging the weather, and improved tracking skills.
DLC expansions added ATV’s and tents and ground blinds. I’m not sure, but it looks as if these can be purchased eventually with in-game funds as an alternative, though it would take a lot of time. Either way, 4 bucks is the cheapest expansion dlc I’ve seen. And, the ATVs are an awesome part of the hunting and exploration. And, the tents allow portable base access; functioning like the permanent outposts throughout the maps. Personally, I’d love to see the addition of boats and fishing. But, that is just a wishlist item. I see no cons to this game.
The game is inspired by the book, Call of the Wild by Jack London. Like the book, the game reveals much about the lives and behaviors of animals, and the great outdoors. Many species are integrated into the world of the current two reserves in Germany and America: Black Bears, Roosevelt Elks, Red Foxes, Coyotes, European Bison, Wild Boar, Moose, Red Deer, Fallow Deer, Roe Deer, Whitetail Deer, and Blacktail Deer. Besides the typical colors, several rare & albino furs appear randomly. The upcoming dlc expansion will add a third reserve in Siberia: Medved, with snow and an anticipated new selection of animals such as the already revealed Lynx.
I was in Scouting myself at an early age, and later an Explorer’s Post as a young adult. I’ve enjoyed the fun of group campouts with my sons in the cub scouts over the course of a decade & the numerous camping trips with families & friends over the years, and even group & solitary hiking & camping experiences. But, I’ve never been hunting myself. As great of an experience as solitary hiking & camping can be, friendship is a huge part of the outdoors. COTW provides a smooth multiplayer experience, where you can either create your own server game, or jump in with already created servers. All outposts & locations unlocked in singleplayer are also available for quick travel on the multiplayer maps. You can join your buddies for group cooperative hunts or compete in challenges.
I get 60fps steady & can play mp with crappy internet. No problems at all. Second monitor & the Steam overlay works great with COTW. You can even open vids in the overlay and listen while you shift/tab back into the game, which is really nice while sitting in a hunting stand in the dark waiting on the animal herd to arrive.
I highly recommend the game for animal lovers, fans of shooters, open sandbox, and sims. The devs at Expansive Worlds have made a high quality game for everyone to love.

I watched the spoilers in their second video because I thought I wouldn't make time to play the game, but this past weekend the game was on sale and I felt like participating in a non-book short story (took me about six hours on Normal). Knowing the ending didn't seem to mar the experience, as I was curious about the telling. I will not include spoilers.
Three Delta operators are dropped on the outskirts of storm-ravaged Dubai, and make their way to the heart of darkness. If that reference is not draw enough, play this game for the novel take on a first-person shooter. Take in the atmospheric city, listen to the humanizing banter of the men you're about to kill, and aim for the head because of the satisfying spray of blood. There is always the decision of whether to keep playing, and if you keep playing there are several decision-points that might have different outcomes. I opted not to find out, and instead played it like a book. Even the ending, when it would be easy to replay the last scene, I left alone.
prompted me to think more about the human condition that any prior gaming experience.
On the mechanics: guns feel and sound solid, voice-acting is well-done, and I didn't notice any glitching in the environment. The fourth wall was only broken when Jenny's number was referenced, but that helped me see this game-world as an alternate version of our world. Set-piece fights sometimes ran long, but I could say the same for the game. As I get older, I value concise experiences. If I were to play it again (not likely, despite the ill-fitted achievement pop-ups from both the game and Steam, and multiplayer makes no sense here. Play CS:GO or Chivalry), I would set the difficulty to Easy, because this is a well-written, interactive narrative.

I always feel sad, reading all those bad reviews from people who probably never read the devblogs even once. For sure ist easy to say, that this game has been in early access for a long time. It is also easy to say, that there is no visible progress.
But that is in fact not the reality. I have been following the devblogs for a long time now and never regreted paying $30 for this game. In fact I see it as an investment for a hopefully great game in the future.
At this point of time the game is definitely not polished, nor is it a lot of fun to play in my oppinion, but it is on a great path to become a superb game.
The developers respect the wishes of their players, they want and accept the help of them in testing the new features and what is most important: They never released a dlc to cash in more Money.
Most games today milk their customers with DLC, Season Pass, Micro-Transactions. DayZ is not one of those Games and I am happy to still have aStudio that stands true to the roots of Gaming.
I want to thank the Developers for all their hard work and hope you show a bit more respect towards them by writing honest reviews instead of just talking the game down without giving meaningful reasons.
You always have to remember, that Steam told you from the start, that this game is in developement and might even never reach the state of release. It is not your average military plot line where you're the 'Murican badass hero here to come save the day from the Russian invasion or a terroist group, thus making the world a happy plus. Spec Ops: The Line? HELL NO. You are no hero. You are simply a soldier, following his orders, not saving the day or rescuing civillians. You make gigantic f**k ups that make you feel like uber sh**. I have a mixed but mostly positive review of this game, graphics and gameplay are both top notch but there are a few issues.
1 VERY annoying crashes, if you thought Skyrim was bad about crashing you have not seen anything yet, these crashes force you to hard reset your computer (aka power buton) because they seem to crash your graphics card and leave you with a blank screen so you cannot even check error messages. Many people have been having this same issue as of the time of this writing.
2 LAG! I am running a premium gaming computer so when I slow down to 4-5 fps there is something in the programing.
3 At points this game can be a little unrealistic, some weapons have extremely poor penetration to the point they are almost useless, shoot a deer at close range with buckshot and you still won't get a vital hit on a big boddied deer makeing shotguns all but useless until you unlock slugs which can take a while since buckshot SUCKS so bad. More ammo choices would be VERY welcome also reforming the TWO ammo choices would be nice, when you need a bullet to penetrate deeper you use a heavier/tougher constructed bullet not use a poly tip which usualy have marginal penetration in real life. they got that totaly backwards in this game.
4 Very limited choice of calibers. No idea how anyone would get the idea to make a hunting game without a 30-06, 308 or 300 Win Mag and entire segments of calibers are missing, no 257 calibers no 6.5mms no 35 calibers no 375s...etc so in terms of power you have to jump streight from a 7mm RM to a freaking 338 Win Mag, also it sucks that you have to jump from a 243 which struggles horribly aginst larger deer to a 270 which has a bad habit of ruining your integrity bonus of your whitetail and blacktail deer, a 257 cal or 6.5mm would make a real nice addition to fill that gap. I personaly own more and a wider variety of hunting firearms then are present in this game.
5 Very limited choice of weapon. No semi auto rifles, no crossbow, no dedicated long range gun.
6 No choke, suppressor, bipod, or muzzle break attachments, those would have been a real nice addition to customize your rifle or maybe even make your shotgun somewhat useful since it scatters WAY too much.
I recommend this game because I really enjoy it despite it's faults, and who knows maybe they will address some of these issues, the game is relativly new after all, and maybe they will consult someone who actualy knowns something about firearms/terminal performace to reform their firearms, hell guys contact me I'll do it for free.

So, what to say about Undertale...
First I should probably state that I have around 100 hours in the game (despite what Steam says, I play a DRM-Free Version of the game for faster loading times).
Personally, I heavily enjoy Undertale but it's definitely not a game for everyone, In my opinion I feel that the moment someone finds out they'll enjoy Undertale is after finishing the first section of the game, the "Ruins" which is actually where the game's demo ends, so If you're conflicted on buying the game, the demo should help you make a decision on whether you'll enjoy the game. I believe this because as the game states, it's the RPG where no one has to die, If the player is attached enough to the first boss, they will try to find a way to spare the first boss or they will kill the first boss and feel guilty. If the player is invested then Undertale is probably for you. If not and you feel like you'll kill whatever you want for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles or whatnot then the game probably won't hook you because making a decision to kill or not to kill plays a big part in Undertale's narrative.
Undertale is a game that's main attraction is the story, If I told you about it though, that would be spoiling the game, so you're just gonna have to take my word for it. Seriously, to quote TotalBiscuit "To explain exactly why Undertale is truly special would require spoiling the experience, so I urge you to look past the hype and just play it yourself."
The gameplay however, while it doesn't compare to the story is pretty decent. The fights with monsters are pretty creative and while the FIGHT mechanic is pretty simple, the ACT mechanic encourages you to evaluate the monster's personality and find a way to make them stop fighting you. Although, most monster's will try to attack you, in this event instead of a classic RPG where it's just RNG based attacks, there is a level of skill added to it. The combat system is a turn-based bullet hell and while I understand this may be hit and miss for some people, I personally enjoyed it.
Yes, the soundtrack is utterly amazing. Even people who don't like the game have exclaimed their love for Undertale's soundtrack. The use of so many different arrangements and instruments fit so well in with the game and also have an enjoyable listening experience outside of the game. Not to mention that such an amazing soundtrack, was made entirely in FL Studio by one person, Toby Fox (The developer of Undertale).
One more thing to know is that this game was made almost entirely by two people, Toby Fox and Temmie Chang, Toby developed most of the game and made the soundtrack while also creating a few of the character's artwork in MS Paint. While Temmie made other characters with GraphicsGale. There were a few other artists who worked on the game, but there contributions were not as big as Toby and Temmie's.
If you do end up liking the game based on the demo, then get ready for a tear-inducing and touching game.
(Just so you know, no matter what anyone tells you, for your first playthrough of the game, play the game exactly how you want to, kill who you feel deserve it and spare who you think don't and then the ending will determine your consequences and what you've done to the monsters' home.)
I'd give Undertale a 10/10, It's a game that's most definitely worth it's ten dollar price tag.

Well DayZ, this review has been a long time coming- and it's finally here.
I bought this game as soon as it hit steam, oh and the joy in my heart when it did. A subtle but satisfying personal Christmas gift I got for myself. I can honestly say I prefer the game it was then, than it is now. Not because it ran any better, or had less bugs. No, it was the sunny optimism behind supporting a game that was right up my alley. If you want a recommendation before I go into my spiel then here it is- No, I do not recommend buying this game. My explanation for that is as follows:
I've had so many good times with this game, a couple hundred hours of exciting gameplay manifested itself in the form of a relatively simple concept. There is no story, there is no "end game", there is no main objective. Except that of Survival. That's what hooked me, and what hooked many others like me. The possibilities are endless in this game, and because of the shoot-on-sight community, your survival is secured by how cold hearted you can be. Now, that never stopped me from helping fellow players. I've done everything from feeding a starving survivor to hitting a half dead waster with defibrillator and giving him a blood transfusion, just to keep him alive a little longer in that harsh world. That being said: I've also had to execute a few bandits, leave some survivors in handcuffs and penny-less in a zombie infested town, and even got my revenge on a hostile player by forcing him to eat his dead comrade. Life in DayZ is a bittersweet symphony that is played by an underground rock band that hipsters pretend to love. Truly the game has so much damn potential it almost brings tears to my eyes to not give it a recommendation. That brings me to the negatives...
I had to explain what I love about the game so you can understand why I can no longer help support it's sales. Numero Uno, The Developers. They made this game on one of the most popular mods in gaming history, DayZ mod for Arma 2. Though it's almost like they couldn't handle a stand alone development, and after releasing an early access game decided to spend their fortune of success instead of making a great game out of the shell. It's been 3 long years of Alpha and no real release in sight. Though, why would they work on a release? Players like me already gave them their money, why waste more time on a few more sales? That's what I feel like the Developers are saying to one another. "We already made our money" Now the community that's left is stuck waiting on the final product, being strung along by small updates and hot fixes. It's a damn shame. That's only the tip of this dirty Iceberg.
Let's talk about how the game plays. Your character is the hungriest and thirstiest son of a gun on the planet. The average human can go up to three weeks without food, and 3 days without water. Your survivor can't go more than an hour on an empty stomach. That is probably my biggest issue with the game, along with the zombies. The zombie AI is glitchy, sometimes they'll notice you from 200 yards away sometimes they can't see you unless you walk right up to them. They can walk through doors that you close behind you for a quick getaway, and they are built like a tank. You can nail a player without a helmet in the noggin with a crowbar and he's out, but a zombie will take 3-4 hits. If those two aspects didn't make the game almost unplayable, the loot system does. Full towns, untouched, might yield enough loot for you and your mate. That's food, water and maybe a gun or two. The loot is so scarce you can never really tell if you're sweeping a town after a group looted it, or if you're just unlucky.
In closing, if you want to support this game and you like zombie survivals then you may or may not enjoy this title. I doubt that you'll have the same experiences I've had because I played it when it was fresh, and the community was excited to help a good game grow. Now it's mostly shoot-on-sight players and hackers.
I give DayZ a very sad, and regretful thumbs down.

I nominated this game for the 2017 Steam Awards for the "Even Better Than I Expected" award. So my review is mostly for the award season, but I'll lay out my thoughts on this game.
Initially, I doubted that I would enjoy this game for some reason. I heard that they were changing the voice actress for Chloe and that the game was going to be a prequel instead of a sequel. Not only that, this game wasn't going to be made by DONTNOD Entertainment, the original developers of Life Is Strange. With all of these changes, I wasn't sure how the game was going to turn out. But boy was I in for a treat.
PROS
- Characters: The greatest driving point of this game are the characters. In this particular game, we take control of Chloe Price and experience what life was at Arcadia Bay before Max returned. We explore her new found relationship with Rachel Amber and the adventures they go on during the course of the game. There is some serious character development for Chloe in this game and it makes you truly feel like you're in Arcadia Bay living as Chloe.
- Story: The story is a nod to the original game, it takes place around the time that Chloe gets expelled from Blackwell, become close friends with Rachel and explore the option of "running away" with Rachel as they mentioned in the original game a lot. As of now of this review, there are only 2 episodes out with the last one coming soon. I will probably update this review again in the future.
- Gameplay: This game plays very similarly to the original game. Choices impacts the story and dialogue presented to the player and surely keeps the pace going steady. They introduced a new dialogue style type of mini-game which I really like and they removed the rewind time function because of obvious reasons.
- Style: Before the Storm obviously looks like the original game, however, I think that this game is a little bit more smoother because it's more current. It's familiar enough to be associated with the first game and yet stylish enough to be able to stand on its own. Definitely a beautiful looking game with the settings on max.
- Length: Each episode so far has been almost 2 hours. For the price of this game, I defintely think that it's worth it and offers you different playthroughs each time you load the game.
- Music: The type of music these use in these games are hauntingly beautiful and fits the atmosphere and setting of the game. Definitely a great soundtrack.
CONS
I don't really have anything negative to say about this game. It's a fun prequel and seriously gives you an insight of how Chloe felt while going through the events of this game. The story is good and makes sense as it connects to the original game and the gameplay is engaging to the point of keeping you hooked. Definintely pick up this game if you're a Life is Strange fan!

The game is pay-to-win. There are special characters with higher distributed attributes than the normal characters (very unfair) and the special characters also start off with better cards (which further increases their attributes). I know this since I had the chance to get a free special character during an event. So don't get mad when you match up against people with special characters and see that they're making 3pt shots in your face the whole game and not missing (*cough* SG...and PF... *cough*).
The game community is extremely toxic. Everyone makes you out to be an amateur (noob) for not being able block EVERY shot from your special 3pt making opponent or not being able to catch a rebound over a tall paid-to-win sasquatch (not literally, but they're pretty big and one of the characters literally looks like a beast). It's either you start off as a pro in this game or face the consequences of being shunned for noobism.
I don't know why entirely, but the server I play in lags every so often even when I have high speed internet connectivity. Anyway, I really did enjoy playing this game during the first few levels, but as you progress, you really start noticing the unfairness and unfriendly playerbase that this game offers.

I picked this game up after seeing a few friends get a lot of enjoyment out of it, but in hindsight I realized that all those friends were depressive and were content to waste away their days with fluff. This game suits that need really well. It has a way of evoking that "one more shot" mentality, making it a quick and dirty time sink, but the content just isn't there to make it worthwhile.
Sure, I haven't explored the different dungeon areas to their fullest extent, but I've seen enough of each room to know that they're just more of the same predictable, bland randomly generated rooms that I was faced with in the opening minutes of the game, albeit with stronger enemies.
Why would I care about fighting stronger enemies? I dunno. The levelling system in this game encourages players to throw themselves at the same challenges over and over until they boost their stats enough to level the playing field, so that they can do it all over again when they reach the next zone. It's a textbook skinner-box game, albeit not quite as synnical and degrading as Farmville.
At the time of writing, I have 101 minutes of playtime and I'm uninstalling this game. In that short amount of time I've seen it all. The randomised dungeons aren't getting any more interesting, I'm seeing the same traits over and over, and the combat isn't engaging or expressive enough to make the combat compelling - even when I get the rare room that evokes the very best of bullet-hell style action and chaos.
This game just really doesn't jive with me, and I find it super hard to recommend, which is a bummer considering this game comes from the same people that did Don't♥♥♥♥♥♥Your Pants - a game much smaller in scope, but managed to give me a lot more satisfaction after much less playtime.
I'm looking forward to seeing what Cellar Door comes out with next. They're clearly a talented and creative studio, but I just feel like they phoned it in on this one.

Really like it, but the reasons for which I like this game might not make much sense so dont mind it.
If you are not patient, or just want an action packed animal shooter, dont like tracking and waiting for long times in a single spot for that perfect albino deer (rare spawn so to say) doing nothing but watching through your binoculars, if you are one of those treehuggers who think hunting is bad, if you dont like to spend literally hours trudging through woods, swamps and  forests, if the lack of a high end goal beyond annoys you (it certainly annoys me at times)...
But above all the first thing mentioned: if you lack patience, do not purchase this game.
Its a very inmersive (maybe not fully realistic but for realism I could buy myself a rifle and go hunting) hunting game with a rather limited variety of animals divided into two BIG hunting reserves.
One in central Europe, and one in northern America (this one rocks).
I think the best comparison I could do about this game is the Silent Hunter submarine simulator games.
In this game you are the hunter, and you got a variety of weapons (rifles and bows substitute the submarines).
Each weapon has some ammo types (torpedoes) which are more adecuated for certain situations (range, target inegrity  etc).
You can freely roam the forests (seas) in search of preys, but obviously you cant just run and gun. Animals (merchants) will spot you and run away or even attack you.
You have to play as a hunter (sorry for being redundant) and lay in wait submerged in the bushes or among the trees, hoping for the prey to make a pass.
Or perhaps you will go into silent navigation (ehrmm I mean stealth mode) and stalk your prey to get close and personal with the bow.
Or try your luck with a long range shot hoping for a kill.
If you miss the shot the animal will run away, and most of the times you will have only one chance to hit him.
If you aim to the weak parts (neck, head, vertebrae) it will be one shot one dead animal.
Or you can hit a non vital part and then youll have to track it (sometimes for a loooong time) till you find the corpse.
Over time your character will get experience points and level up, allowing you to unlock a series of perks and weapon skills that will help you further in your endeavours.
There are four types of weapons: bows, rifles, shotguns and revolvers, but I have to say that the amount of weapons available in game is rather poor.
You can spend your credits (earned via hunting or doing missions) in those weapons, aswell as gear such as animal attractors, backpacks, tents or some all terrain motorbike.
And obviously ammo, which aint free.
Right now the problem I got with the game is that there aint much to do with the credits you earn once you got the gear from the shop.
Also, the variety of species aint very big (each or the two hunting reserves has its own fauna).
Being a hunting game would be great to be able to set up a camp with a small fire, even if it only serves an inmersion purpose.
All in all I recommend it as long as you meet the patience requirement.
